title: Scott Bessent & Paul Atkins: Holdings & Divestiture Deadlines
summary: Bessent missed his divestiture deadline, which the Office of Government Ethics documented in an 11 Aug 2025 letter to the Senate Finance Committee: the deadline was 28 April 2025 and his first certification showed only partial compliance. He then amended his ethics agreement three times, kept three private holdings with Treasury's approval, and in December 2025 exchanged his North Dakota farmland for a $5M-$25M non-recourse note from the buyer. He certified full compliance on 5 Dec 2025. Atkins certified on 18 Jul 2025 that all his divestitures, including Patomak, were done on time, with no waivers; the Patomak buyer has not been made public. Claims that either man's decisions (China soybean deals, farm aid, the Argentina swap, SEC case dismissals) served his own holdings, former clients or friends are allegations: no authority has found a conflict, and the one review on record (Treasury OIG, on a mis-reported JPMorgan stake) found no knowing violation.

sub_claims.statement: Scott Bessent disclosed Key Square Group, North Dakota farmland and other assets and agreed to divest them within 90 days of confirmation.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (nominee OGE 278e and ethics agreement, both read in full). Bessent's nominee report (signed 28 Dec 2024) lists Key Square Group LP, the investment firm he founded, valued at over $50 million, with $2,787,000 in management fees and incentive allocations plus a $1,041,134 guaranteed payment; Key Square funds holding S&P 500 and Nasdaq ETFs, currency positions and put options (each line 'over $50,000,000' or $1M-$25M); iShares Bitcoin Trust ($250K-$500K); and High Plains Acres LLP, holding farmland in Burleigh, Kidder, Eddy, Benson and Wells counties, North Dakota, valued at $5,000,001-$25,000,000 with $100,001-$1,000,000 of rent tied to corn and soybean prices. The ethics agreement of 9 Jan 2025 committed him to resign from Key Square on confirmation, divest his partnership share within 90 days, and stay out of specific-party matters involving Key Square for one year; and to divest 25 listed holdings within 90 days, among them High Plains Acres, the Key Square funds, IBIT, Verizon, Archer Daniels Midland, GLD, open currency positions, Greengage Global Holding, Aperion (DE) Feeder Fund, Presight RV Co-Invest Fund, Half Acre WSW and Cambrian Biopharma. Three hedge-fund interests (Totem Macro, Totem Management Seed, Old Farm Partners) were to be redeemed quarterly, finishing by September 2025. He kept several family LLCs and trusts with a recusal commitment. He was confirmed on 27 Jan 2025.

sub_claims.statement: The Office of Government Ethics told the Senate that Bessent missed his divestiture deadline.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (OGE letters read in full). On 11 Aug 2025 OGE's Deputy Director for Compliance, Dale Christopher, notified Senate Finance Chairman Mike Crapo under Program Advisory PA-19-09 that Bessent 'has failed to timely comply with certain terms' of his ethics agreement: he had to comply with certain provisions by 28 April 2025 and certify by 5 May 2025. He submitted a certification on 5 May 'indicating partial compliance'; that form, signed 2 May, ticks 'No' on completing divestitures and says divestitures 'have been initiated but not yet completed for all assets' and no 278-T had been filed. OGE wrote that a further amendment was needed and 'there is currently no timeline for resolution', and that it had advised Treasury ethics officials to emphasise that avoiding conflicts with his holdings was his personal responsibility. On 13 Aug 2025 OGE added that Treasury said Bessent was committed to completing the remaining divestitures by 15 Dec 2025, that the assets were 'illiquid and are not readily marketable', and that he had been and would remain recused from matters affecting them, with a screening memorandum given to his front office. A missed deadline documented by OGE is a fact; OGE's letters do not find that he took part in any conflicting matter.

sub_claims.statement: Bessent's divestitures were completed, partly through amendments that extended deadlines or let him keep assets.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (278-Ts, certifications, amendments and 2026 annual report, read in full). (a) The 278-T signed 14 Jul 2025 shows Key Square Group LP and Key Square Partners II sales between 11 Feb and 25 Mar 2025, Old Farm Partners (28 Jan, 24 Apr), Roxo Energy Funding IV (25 Mar, $850K-$1.75M by range), GLD and Verizon (4 Mar 2025), Totem Macro (27 Mar, 30 Jun) and others: 24 transactions. (b) Amendment of 5 Jun 2025: Treasury's ethics official found that Presight RV Co-Invest Fund, Half Acre WSW (Waterloo Sparkling Water) and Cambrian Biopharma posed no conflict risk; Bessent keeps them with a recusal commitment (the 2026 report shows them still held: Half Acre $1M-$5M, Cambrian $750K-$1.5M across two series, Presight $50K-$100K). (c) Follow-up certification of 3 Oct 2025: Totem holdings finalised. (d) Amendment signed by Bessent in early December and forwarded by Treasury on 8 Dec 2025: he 'was unable to divest these entities within 90 days of my confirmation due to their illiquid nature' and would divest Greengage and Aperion and cause High Plains Acres to sell its farmland by 15 Dec 2025 in exchange for a promissory note, with no equity taken back on default, and recusal from matters affecting the buyer's ability to repay and from specific-party matters involving the buyer until paid. (e) 278-T signed 5 Dec 2025: Totem Management Seed sold 23 Sep 2025 ($250K-$500K), Greengage 27 Nov 2025. (f) Final certification signed 5 Dec 2025: 'All required divestitures are now completed', no waivers or authorizations. (g) 2026 annual report: Apeiron sold 2 Dec 2025; ADM sold 4 Mar 2025; High Plains Acres now holds only bank accounts and a 'non-recourse note exchanged for farmland' from Glacier Ridge, LLP valued at $5,000,001-$25,000,000, and Bessent is listed as a partner of High Plains Acres from 11/2025. So the farmland was exchanged for a seller-financed note about 7.5 months after the original deadline; the economic interest now runs through a note secured, as reported, by the same land. Who controls Glacier Ridge, LLP is not public in what we found.

sub_claims.statement: Bessent publicly announced the farmland divestment, after earlier calling himself a soybean farmer during China trade talks.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented (AP, read in full via syndication; filings). In October 2025, while leading trade talks with China, Bessent told ABC News 'I'm actually a soybean farmer' and 'I have felt this pain too' (AP). On 30 Oct 2025 he announced that China had agreed to buy 12 million metric tons of US soybeans in the current season and 25 million tons a year for three years (AP, Agri-Pulse; excerpts). On 7 Dec 2025 he said on CBS's 'Face the Nation': 'I actually just divested it this week as part of my ethics agreement, so I'm out of that business.' A $12 billion farm aid package was announced at the White House on 8 Dec. The New York Times (quoted by Tri-State Livestock News) reported it found no record of a divestment at the time and that North Dakota records listed Bessent's husband, John Freeman, as a managing partner of High Plains Acres. The OGE filings later posted show the farmland was exchanged for a note under the December amendment. Older summaries saying he had divested in October 2025 are wrong.

sub_claims.statement: Bessent's farmland or other holdings created a conflict with China trade, farm aid or tariff decisions.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: allegation. Campaign Legal Center (9 Jul 2025) asked OGE to investigate whether Bessent violated 18 U.S.C. 208, citing S&P 500 funds and Verizon and ADM; CLC and Democracy Defenders Fund (13 and 20 Aug 2025) asked OGE and the Treasury Inspector General to investigate, arguing that his role in talks with China and Canada while holding the farmland 'creates a serious risk of a financial conflict'. Context that cuts against parts of the complaint: the later 278-T and annual report show Verizon, GLD and ADM were sold on 4 Mar 2025 and the Key Square funds by March 2025, so the July complaint's premise that those were undivested was not borne out by the filings once posted (they had not been public when CLC wrote). Section 208 covers 'particular matters', and broad trade policy is usually not one; whether any specific decision affected High Plains Acres directly and predictably has not been assessed publicly. Treasury told OGE he was recused from matters affecting the undivested assets. No OGE, Inspector General or court finding of a violation was found as of Nov 2026. The only finding on record runs the other way on a narrower point: the 2026 annual report notes that his spouse's JPMorgan stock was mis-reported as a bank deposit, sold in July 2025 once noticed, a $200 late fee was paid, and 'the Office of the Inspector General reviewed the situation and determined that there was no knowing violation' of the Ethics in Government Act or 18 U.S.C. 208, with the ethics official concurring.

sub_claims.statement: The $20 billion Argentina support package benefited investors linked to Bessent's former colleagues.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: the package and the investors' positions are documented or reported; benefit-by-design is an allegation. Treasury announced support on 22 Sep 2025 and in mid-October signed a $20 billion exchange stabilization agreement with Argentina's central bank, drawing $2.5 billion in pesos; Treasury says Argentina fully repaid in December 2025 and the ESF holds no pesos, but the agreement was not shown to be terminated (Warren letter of 4 Feb 2026, read in full, quoting Treasury's 20 Jan 2026 reply and the ESF December 2025 notes). Mother Jones and Popular Information reported that Rob Citrone of Discovery Capital, a friend and former Soros colleague of Bessent, held large Argentine positions; Argentine press reported he lobbied Bessent. The New York Times reported that Stanley Druckenmiller, another former Soros colleague, was also invested and said he had no communication with Bessent about Argentina before or after the announcement; a Citrone spokesman declined to comment (NYT, seen only in a search summary). Neither man is a documented former client of Bessent's, and Key Square's one-year specific-party bar covered Key Square itself, not former colleagues. Warren and Shaheen (17 Dec 2025) and Warren (6 Nov 2025, 4 Feb 2026) sought the terms and the list of interested investors; Treasury's replies did not provide the agreement. No Inspector General or GAO review of the swap was found; the Treasury OIG's January 2026 report is a routine audit of the ESF's financial statements. Bessent says the package was not a bailout and that Treasury made money.

sub_claims.statement: Paul Atkins disclosed Patomak Global Partners, crypto-related interests and his wife's family wealth, and agreed to divest.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: documented for the ethics agreement (read in full); the nominee report's figures are as reported (the report itself is released only on request). The agreement of 20 Mar 2025 commits Atkins to resign as chief executive of Patomak Global Partners on confirmation, forfeit post-confirmation distributions and divest his membership interest within 90 days; to stay out of specific-party matters involving Patomak for one year after resigning and involving any former client for one year after his last service to it; to divest vested Securitize options (he had resigned from Securitize in Feb 2025) and Pontoro equity within 90 days; to divest 30 listed holdings (Attachment A, including Anchor Labs, Inc., the parent of Anchorage Digital, and bank and big-tech stocks) and 18 sector funds within 90 days, and 92 private funds (Attachment B, including Off the Chain LP) within 120 days. He keeps stock in TAMKO Holdings, Inc.; his spouse is an employee of TAMKO Building Products, LLC with a profit-sharing plan, and he remains trustee of seven family trusts, all with recusal commitments. He resigned from The Digital Chamber and its Token Alliance in December 2024. Reported values: Securitize options $250K-$500K, Anchorage equity $250K-$500K, Off the Chain Capital $1M-$5M, about $6M of crypto-related assets in all (Fortune, The Block); Atkins and his wife together worth at least $327 million, with the Patomak stake at least $25 million (Bloomberg Law). Disclosed Patomak clients include FalconX, Virtu, Temasek, the Options Clearing Corporation, Bank of America, Barclays and Exxon Mobil, with four clients withheld as confidential (Bloomberg Law, Rolling Stone; excerpts).

Grade: documented (certification read in full; OGE index). Atkins was confirmed on 9 Apr 2025, so the 90-day deadline fell on 8 Jul 2025 and the 120-day deadline on 7 Aug 2025. His certification, signed 18 Jul 2025 (due 14 Aug), ticks 'Yes' for completing all resignations before taking office and all divestitures within the time specified, cites 278-Ts filed 28 Jun and 18 Jul 2025, states he forfeited Patomak distributions after confirmation, and reports no 18 U.S.C. 208 waiver and no 5 C.F.R. 2635.502(d) authorization. OGE's index lists two Certificates of Divestiture for him (OGE-2025-099 posted 20 May 2025 and OGE-2025-160 posted 25 Jul 2025), a third 278-T posted 18 Nov 2025 and a 2026 annual report posted 26 Aug 2026; these are released only on written request and were not read. No OGE notice of non-compliance was found. Warren (5 Aug 2025) asked him to name the buyers and prices for Patomak and the other 140 assets and to explain how he could certify on 18 Jul before the 120-day date; no public reply was found, and the Patomak buyer is still not public. A report that he sold the stake for $25M-$50M was seen only in a search summary and is unverified. The SEC says he is upholding the commitments in his ethics agreement.

sub_claims.statement: SEC decisions under Atkins touched former Patomak clients or his former holdings, and he recused where required.
sub_claims.finding: Grade: the decisions are documented; a benefit to a former client through Atkins's participation is not. (a) Devon Archer: the SEC stipulated to dismiss its civil case against Archer with prejudice on or about 18 Sep 2025 after Trump's pardon (SEC release, Law360; excerpts). The New York Times reported that in 2018 Archer's lawyers paid Atkins $1,450 an hour as an expert witness, and an Atkins spokesperson said he recused himself from the decision (via Political Wire and Cryptonews; single-source chain, the NYT article was not read). Service in 2018 falls outside his one-year former-client bar, so the recusal as reported went beyond the agreement. (b) The SEC dismissed seven dealer-registration cases in mid-2025, including the case against John Fife (White & Case, read in full); one search summary described Fife as a disclosed Atkins client, which we could not confirm, so it is unverified. (c) Securitize, a former holding, had its SPAC registration declared effective on 5 Jun 2026, after Atkins's one-year bar lapsed (Feb 2026) and long after he divested (see the Securitize-Cantor check). (d) Crypto enforcement dismissals (Binance, Kraken, Ripple and others) are recorded in earlier checks; none of those firms is a documented Patomak client (FalconX is; no FalconX enforcement action was found). (e) Barron's reported in Aug 2025 that defendants in a Trump Media lawsuit sought Patomak records; Trump Media called this meritless and denied engaging Patomak. Warren called the pattern of dismissals 'open corruption'; Blumenthal (30 Mar 2026) asked for records of crypto settlements. No recusal list is published by the SEC, no waiver is on record, and no authority has found that Atkins took part in a matter he should have avoided.

corrections: Claimed (C65): Bessent 'said in Oct 2025 that he had divested' the farmland. The record shows: in October 2025 he said 'I'm actually a soybean farmer'; he announced the divestment on CBS on 7 Dec 2025, and OGE filings show the land was exchanged for a non-recourse promissory note from Glacier Ridge, LLP ($5M-$25M) under an ethics-agreement amendment with a 15 Dec 2025 deadline.

Claimed (C65): 'about $25M of North Dakota farmland'. The record shows: the nominee report values the farmland at $5,000,001-$25,000,000 (a range; $25M is the ceiling), with $100,001-$1,000,000 of crop-linked rent.

Claimed (C54): Atkins held 'about $1M of Anchorage Digital equity' and 'Securitize call options worth $2.5-5M'. The record shows: reported ranges are $250K-$500K for Anchorage (Anchor Labs, Inc.) and $250K-$500K for the Securitize options, plus $1M-$5M in Off the Chain Capital; C65 already uses the lower figures.

Claimed (C54): disclosure showed 'up to ~$327M in family assets'. The record shows: Bloomberg Law's headline says Atkins and his wife are worth 'at least $327 million'; the bound depends on how the ranges are summed, so 'at least' is the reported wording.

Claimed (C54, C65): no buyer for Patomak is public. Still true as of Nov 2026; add that Atkins certified full compliance on 18 Jul 2025 with no waivers or authorizations, and that OGE issued him two Certificates of Divestiture (OGE-2025-099, OGE-2025-160).

Claimed (CLC complaint, Jul 2025): Bessent had failed to divest Verizon and Archer Daniels Midland. The record shows: both were sold on 4 Mar 2025, though this became public only after the complaint (278-T of 14 Jul 2025 and the 2026 annual report).

Warren's letter of 5 Aug 2025 puts Atkins's 90-day mark at 9 Jul 2025; counting from confirmation on 9 Apr 2025 it falls on 8 Jul 2025. OGE puts Bessent's 90-day deadline at 28 Apr 2025; CLC used 27 Apr.
denials_and_context: Treasury told OGE that Bessent had worked to divest since January 2025, that the remaining assets were illiquid and restricted, and that he was and would remain recused from matters affecting them. Bessent said in August 2025 that he had sold about 96% of what he had to divest (as reported by The New York Times, cited in the DDF/CLC letter).

Treasury's ethics official certified each Bessent filing as compliant with applicable laws, and the final certification of 5 Dec 2025 states all required divestitures were completed. The Treasury OIG found no knowing violation over the mis-reported JPMorgan stock.
Sen. Ron Wyden said the Treasury secretary was picking and choosing which ethics requirements to follow (as reported by Banking Dive). No public statement from Sen. Crapo was found.

Bessent says the Argentina package was not a bailout and that Treasury profited; Treasury says the $2.5B draw was fully repaid in December 2025. Druckenmiller says he did not communicate with Bessent about Argentina; a Citrone spokesman declined to comment.

The SEC says Atkins takes his obligations seriously and is upholding the commitments in his ethics agreement; an Atkins spokesperson said he recused from the Archer dismissal. Trump Media called the Patomak subpoena effort meritless.

Holding an asset, or a decision that helps a former employer, client or colleague, is not by itself a violation. 18 U.S.C. 208 applies to particular matters with a direct and predictable effect on the official's own or imputed interests; the impartiality rule (5 C.F.R. 2635.502) covers former employers and clients for one year. Neither covers friends or former colleagues.

Research note: Atkins's nominee report, 278-Ts and annual report are released only on written request to OGE and were not read; his figures come from press reports. A full-text New York Times article on the Archer recusal and on Druckenmiller was not read.

leads.why_connected: Bessent's partnership holds a $5M-$25M non-recourse note from it; his amended ethics agreement bars him from matters affecting the buyer's ability to repay. Its owners and any link to the Bessent family or tenants are not public.
